# The Whole-Tone Return

## #0 — State the interval body

The [core spine](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) derives the ratio body around the doubled fourth `16/9`. The [musical derivation house](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-ql-musical-derivation-v3/taylor-2026-ql-musical-derivation-v3.md) develops its octave remainder. The [Scholtz house](../../episteme/sources/mathematics-logic/scholtz/scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings/scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings.md) supplies the exact Pythagorean tuning context.

The inputs are positive frequency ratios: fourth `4/3`, fifth `3/2`, octave `2`. Successive intervals multiply their ratios; the interval between two ratios is their quotient.

## #1 — Derive the missing interval

Two fourths give `(4/3)²=16/9`. To reach the octave, solve `(16/9)r=2`. Division gives `r=2·9/16=9/8`. Thus

`(16/9)(9/8)=2`.

This remainder is multiplicative. Subtracting the scalar ratios gives `2−16/9=2/9`, a different quantity. The native “one tone short” names the quotient relation, not an arithmetic difference of frequencies independent of the starting pitch.

## #2 — Recover it between fourth and fifth

The fifth divided by the fourth gives `(3/2)/(4/3)=9/8`. At a 240 Hz reference, the fourth is 320 Hz and the fifth 360 Hz. Their frequency difference is 40 Hz, while their interval ratio is 360/320=9/8. At a 480 Hz reference the difference doubles to 80 Hz, but the interval remains 9/8.

The doubled fourth above 240 Hz is `1280/3` Hz. Multiplying by 9/8 gives 480 Hz, the octave. The same interval therefore links two distinct constructions while retaining their input frequencies.

## #3 — Name the dependence of the third reading

The musical source also writes `2·6²/2⁶=72/64=9/8`. This is the doubled 36 component divided by 64. Since the base ratio is 64/36, this is algebraically the same octave-residue operation `2/(64/36)`. Its native double-cover reading adds an interpretive office; it is not an independent arithmetic proof unrelated to the first route.

The eight foundational ratios retain both directions: `1`, `4/3`, `3/4`, `3/2`, `2/3`, `16/9`, `9/8`, `2`. [Music's ratio page](../music/foundational-ratios.md) places them in the full circuit.

## #4 — Preserve the pure/tempered distinction

Six pure 9/8 tones multiply to `531441/262144`, which exceeds 2. Their ratio to an octave is the [Pythagorean comma](pythagorean-comma.md), `531441/524288`. A six-step whole-tone cycle in twelve-tone equal temperament instead uses `2^(1/6)` per step and closes exactly after six steps.

The pure remainder and tempered pitch-class traversal are related musical constructions with different exact ratios. The native generative remainder is preserved by stating this distinction, not by making the two generators numerically identical.

## #5→0 — Return through the interval that remains

The result is an exact completion relation: the achieved 16/9 requires 9/8 to reach 2. Its native reading makes the remainder a condition for renewed movement. The arithmetic establishes the ratio; the ontological meaning of return belongs to the authorial derivation.
